findings.issue_text: [High/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java:452 — searchForUser() drops the .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) from the search stream. When the caller cannot view users and auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set (admin with only query-users, no admin-permissions resource server, or cross-realm admin), no UserModel.GROUPS attribute is set and the raw search result is returned unfiltered — every realm user is disclosed where previously all were filtered out. The PR's own test (GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers, initial assertTrue(search.isEmpty())) contradicts this change and would fail.

[High/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~112-116 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses groupResource.getId() (the authorization Resource's UUID) both in hasPermission(...) and in granted.add(...). Group resources are named with the Keycloak group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId()), and hasPermission resolves via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so passing the UUID misses the resource, silently falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set contains authz UUIDs instead of group IDs. The UserModel.GROUPS session filter then receives invalid IDs, breaking group-based user search/count (and, combined with issue 1, leaving it unrestricted). groupResource.getName() must be used in both places.

[High/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~64 — canManage() checks hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a caller granted only the view scope on all-groups satisfies requireManage() (e.g., group creation via GroupsResource.add). This contradicts the GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() javadoc ("permission to MANAGE the group") and the per-group canManage(group), which correctly checks MANAGE only — a view→manage privilege escalation.

[Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~170-211 (+ AdminPermissions.java:73-97) — V2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions, but these are still reachable from shared code: the GroupRemovedEvent listener registered by AdminPermissions calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on every group deletion, so group deletion fails with a 500 whenever the V2 evaluator (MgmtPermissionsV2) is selected; conversely, if the listener is not registered (V1 feature off), V2 group resources are never cleaned up and accumulate as orphans. The group management/permissions REST endpoints hit the same UOE.

[Medium/data] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~99 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() never short-circuits for a type-level (all-groups) VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant. A caller permitted to view members of all groups should get an empty set (unrestricted search), but the method only enumerates groups that already have resource entries; when an all-groups grant coexists with any per-group resource, the returned set is non-empty and user search/count is wrongly restricted to members of the enumerated groups, hiding all other users.

[Low/doc_defect] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~120 — requireManageMembers(GroupModel) javadoc says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false; it must reference canManageMembers(GroupModel) (copy-paste error).

[Low/doc_defect] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~132 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() javadoc declares @return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission, but the method returns Set<String>.

[Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — no negative test asserts that a caller granted only VIEW (not MANAGE) on all-groups cannot create/manage groups, so the canManage() escalation (issue 3) goes undetected by the suite.

[Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — no test exercises group deletion while group permissions/resources exist, so the broken V2 cleanup path via the GroupRemovedEvent listener (issue 4) is untested.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java:452 — searchForUser() drops the .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) from the search stream. When the caller cannot view users and auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set (admin with only query-users, no admin-permissions resource server, or cross-realm admin), no UserModel.GROUPS attribute is set and the raw search result is returned unfiltered — every realm user is disclosed where previously all were filtered out. The PR's own test (GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers, initial assertTrue(search.isEmpty())) contradicts this change and would fail.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `services/.../UsersResource.java` removes the explicit `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw stream directly to `toRepresentation(...)`. At the same time, it no longer gates the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute on `!auth.users().canView()`: it only sets it when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. When the caller cannot view users and `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set (e.g., no granted groups, cross-realm, or no resource server per `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` returning `Collections.emptySet()`), no restriction attribute is set and the search stream is no longer filtered by `canView`, so previously-hidden users can be returned. This matches the finding’s disclosure scenario and would contradict the new test’s expectation that the initial search is empty.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~170-211 (+ AdminPermissions.java:73-97) — V2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions, but these are still reachable from shared code: the GroupRemovedEvent listener registered by AdminPermissions calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on every group deletion, so group deletion fails with a 500 whenever the V2 evaluator (MgmtPermissionsV2) is selected; conversely, if the listener is not registered (V1 feature off), V2 group resources are never cleaned up and accumulate as orphans. The group management/permissions REST endpoints hit the same UOE.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GroupPermissionsV2 where multiple GroupPermissionManagement methods (e.g., isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. In the same diff, AdminPermissions.registerListener (when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled) registers a listener that, on GroupRemovedEvent, calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false). MgmtPermissionsV2 now overrides groups() to return GroupPermissionsV2, so under V2 this event path will invoke GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) and throw UOE, which would surface as a 500 during group deletion/event handling. This reachability is directly shown by the added override in MgmtPermissionsV2 and the unchanged listener call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~99 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() never short-circuits for a type-level (all-groups) VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant. A caller permitted to view members of all groups should get an empty set (unrestricted search), but the method only enumerates groups that already have resource entries; when an all-groups grant coexists with any per-group resource, the returned set is non-empty and user search/count is wrongly restricted to members of the enumerated groups, hiding all other users.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the method only builds a set by iterating `resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and adding IDs for which `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)` is true. There is no early check for a type-level (all-groups) grant such as `hasPermission(null, VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)` that should make the returned set empty (meaning “no restriction”). Because `hasPermission(...)` explicitly falls back to the resource-type resource when a per-group resource is missing, a type-level VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant can make the per-resource check return true for the enumerated resources, yielding a non-empty set. Downstream code (`UsersResource.searchForUser` / `getUsersCount`, and similarly in `BruteForceUsersResource`) treats a non-empty set as a restriction (sets `UserModel.GROUPS` / passes the set), which would incorrectly limit user search/count even though the caller has all-groups members-view permission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~120 — requireManageMembers(GroupModel) javadoc says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false; it must reference canManageMembers(GroupModel) (copy-paste error).

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionEvaluator, the Javadoc above `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false, but the method name indicates it should correspond to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` (a copy/paste doc error). This is a verifiable documentation issue in the diff, not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~132 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() javadoc declares @return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission, but the method returns Set<String>.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionEvaluator, the method signature is `Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission();` but the newly added Javadoc directly above it says `@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.` This is a concrete, diff-verifiable documentation mismatch (Set vs Stream), but it does not affect runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — no negative test asserts that a caller granted only VIEW (not MANAGE) on all-groups cannot create/manage groups, so the canManage() escalation (issue 3) goes undetected by the suite.

adjudication.rationale: The new test suite exercises all-groups VIEW in `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewGroups()` only for listing groups (expects size 2 after `createAllGroupsPermission(..., Set.of(VIEW))`), but it does not assert that VIEW-only all-groups cannot create/update/subgroup/map-roles. This is relevant because the diff adds new group permission logic in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` that treats all-groups `VIEW` as sufficient (`hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`), so a regression/escalation in manage checks would not be caught by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — no test exercises group deletion while group permissions/resources exist, so the broken V2 cleanup path via the GroupRemovedEvent listener (issue 4) is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a potentially fragile cleanup path: `AdminPermissions.registerListener` handles `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false)`, but `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` now returns `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(...)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` ("Not supported in V2"). The newly added `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` creates groups and permissions but does not delete a group while permissions/resources exist, so this event-driven cleanup behavior (and its V2 breakage) is indeed unexercised by tests in the diff.
